title: Why Ryt Bank set up Amplitude before it had its first customer
summary: How Ryt Bank uses behavioral data to run its AI assistant, earn customer trust, and scale to 1.5 million users in Malaysia.
body_markdown:
**Insights/Action/Outcome**


Ryt Bank put Amplitude in place before welcoming its first customer so it could understand behavior from day one. Today, those insights help the bank improve Ryt AI, measure meaningful customer engagement, and give product managers the tools to investigate questions independently as the bank grows.


---


I head product at[Ryt Bank](https://www.rytbank.my/) , an AI-powered digital bank licensed and regulated by Bank Negara Malaysia. Our ambition is to make everyday banking simpler and more useful by understanding what customers need.


[Ryt AI](https://www.rytbank.my/ryt-ai) , our banking assistant, is central to that approach. Customers can complete transfers and bill payments by typing what they need in Bahasa Malaysia or English. To improve that experience, we need to understand how people use it, where they find value, and where they need more support.


## **Building the foundation from day one**


When we started building Ryt Bank, we made an important decision: we wanted to understand how customers would use our bank from the very first day. That meant putting analytics in place before we even had our first customer.


Our philosophy was simple: you can always improve a product, but you can’t go back and capture customer behavior you never measured. By setting up Amplitude early, we could learn from our first customers and use those insights as we developed the banking experience.


Amplitude is where our product, growth, product marketing, and engineering teams go to understand customer behavior, feature by feature. It gives our teams a shared view of how customers are actually using the product, while our warehouse and BI remain the financial source of truth. They’re complementary systems that help us answer different questions.


> “Amplitude gives our teams a shared view of how customers are actually using the product. Our warehouse and BI remain the financial source of truth. They’re complementary systems that help us answer different questions.”


Kevin Ong


Head of Product, Ryt Bank


## **Using behavioral data to improve AI banking**


Ryt AI uses multiple specialized agents to handle different banking needs. A customer’s entry point provides useful context: someone arriving from customer support usually needs something fixed, which has a narrower scope than someone opening a blank chat. We pass that context to the assistant to help route the request appropriately.


Behavioral data helps us understand which requests customers make most often, where they complete their tasks, and where they get stuck. We use those insights to prioritize improvements, particularly for requests with high volume and low completion. We also use behavioral context to inform how much information a human agent receives during an interaction.


## **Understanding how customers find value in Ryt AI**


Understanding where customers get stuck also means understanding when they feel comfortable using Ryt AI for a transaction. Trust in the assistant isn’t universal. AI-savvy customers feel comfortable using Ryt AI to bank from the get-go. Others need some reassurance before they’ll let an assistant move their money, no matter how easy it is.


Customers who complete at least one transfer with Ryt AI show double the 30-day transacting retention of customers who never use it. That association helps us understand how meaningful use of the assistant connects with ongoing engagement, and where to focus our onboarding improvements.


We measure the share of users who get real, tangible value from Ryt AI, based on concrete activities: making a transfer, paying a bill, getting a question answered, etc. About 78% of monthly Ryt AI users clear that bar in a given month.


We also track how quickly customers complete their first useful task with Ryt AI. It used to take days, but now, thanks to onboarding experiments and a better introduction to the assistant, the median time from account creation to a first AI-completed task is 19 hours.


## **Growing to 1.5 million users without losing the thread**


Reaching 1.5 million users within a year of public launch was an important milestone. To understand where we were delivering value, we needed to look beyond sign-ups to how customers actually used the bank.


> “At Ryt Bank, a shared taxonomy means everyone starts from the same definitions, so conversations skip straight to what to do next.”


Kevin Ong


Head of Product, Ryt Bank


Growing that fast throws a lot of variables at a team at once. Figuring out which channels are working, where product-market fit is strongest, and what to prioritize next isn’t easy in the moment. Making sure that every team is working from the same picture helps.


At Ryt Bank, a shared taxonomy means everyone starts from the same definitions, so conversations skip straight to what to do next.


## **Using insights to make faster decisions**


Setting up dashboards can be time-consuming. With[Amplitude MCP](https://amplitude.com/mcp-server) , dashboards come together with the right context built in, so the team can move more quickly from understanding what happened to deciding what to do next.


PMs also run their own analysis with Amplitude. Testing a hunch in ten minutes changes what questions you even think to ask. To some extent, the data analyst and product roles have merged here. A PM at Ryt Bank is expected to answer their own questions about customer behavior, and that’s changed what the job looks like.


## **The next chapter**


Looking ahead, we see an opportunity to apply the same approach to a broader range of banking needs, including those of small and medium businesses.


Business banking brings a different level of complexity. A retailer that settles daily and a services firm that invoices monthly may hold the same account type but have different needs around payments, payroll, reconciliation, and cash flow.


As we explore those needs, we want to understand which problems customers encounter most often and how well we address them.


## **Building a bank that keeps learning**


Putting analytics in place before our first customer gave us a way to learn from the beginning. As Ryt Bank grows, our priorities remain the same: understand customer behavior, identify real needs, and use those insights to improve the banking experience. Amplitude gives our teams a shared foundation for that work, whether we’re improving a customer’s first interaction with Ryt AI or exploring what a business needs from its bank.


> “Our priorities remain the same: understand customer behavior, identify real needs, and use those insights to improve the banking experience.”


Kevin Ong


Head of Product, Ryt Bank
